input.quote: The Licensee shall calculate the license fee payable to the Licensor for each month based on the Monthly Notional Volume bands for that pay period and shall pay the Licensor accordingly.
input.rationale: The fee architecture is purely usage-based and meets the preferred position: user fees are a tiered rate "per US$1million traded (for each one-way part of the trade)" applied to actual Monthly Notional Volume (p0056–p0058, p0070). A full-text review found no minimum purchase commitment, no committed volume, no take-or-pay, no shortfall or make-whole payment, and no volume cap on Licensee's usage — searches for "minimum", "commit", "shall be no less than" and "per month" return nothing of that character. The only fixed amounts are the already-advanced $35,000 initial payment (p0051) and $2,500 per month for Technical Support Services (p0086), which are fees for ordered services rather than a purchase commitment. The volume tiers operate only to reduce the per-million rate as volume rises, so higher volume benefits us. The "In no event shall the amount payable ... be less than the amount recorded ... as being traded" language in p0070 is a floor tied to actual recorded trades, not a committed minimum. Noted for context only (not a deviation under this rule): the initial term is 36 months and renewal is at Licensor's option (p0049) — term/renewal control is addressed under the term and termination rules, not as a take-or-pay exposure, since no spend is committed over that term. No redline proposed.
